L112: ## 2. Image Values: the cite19†<image> type
L113: 
L114: The cite19†<image> value type denotes a 2D image. It can be a cite39†url reference or a cite42†color gradient . Its syntax is:

L118: An cite19†<image> can be used in many CSS properties, including the cite84†background-image , cite87†list-style-image , cite86†cursor properties cite20†[CSS2] (where it replaces the cite21†<url> component in the property’s value).
L119: In some cases an image is invalid, such as a cite21†<url> pointing to a resource that is not a valid image format or that has failed to load. L124: ### 2.1. Image References: the cite107†url() notation
L125: 
L126: The simplest way to indicate an image is to reference an image file by URL. This can be done with the cite107†url() notation, defined in cite85†[CSS-VALUES-3] .

L128: In the example below, a background image is specified with cite107†url() syntax:

L131: If the UA cannot download, parse, or otherwise successfully display the contents at the URL as an image (i.e. if the image is not fully cite108†fully decodable†html.spec.whatwg.org ) it must be treated as an cite99†invalid image .
L132: #### 2.1.1. Ambiguous Reference-or-Image URLs
L133: 
L134: URLs are used in many contexts for many types of resources, and therefore can be interpreted in many ways. Usually the context the URL appears in makes it clear how to interpret the resource, but in some instances it can be ambiguous. For example, a cite109†mask-image cite21†<url> value pointing to an SVG file could be interpreted as a reference to an element in the file or as an cite19†<image> .
L135: An ambiguous image URL is a cite21†<url> value that can be interpreted as either an cite19†<image> or an element reference. If an cite110†ambiguous image URL is a cite111†fragment-only URL , then it must be treated as an element reference.
L136: Otherwise, if the ambiguous image URL has a fragment that references an element in the resource that is an appropriate type of element for the context in which the <url> appears (such as a `cite112†mask ` element for the cite109†mask-image property), it is interpreted as an element reference. Otherwise, it is treated as an <image>.
L137: Specs using the cite110†ambiguous image URL concept must define what elements are valid references for the URL, and any additional conditions that might apply.
L138: 
L139: For example, a reference like cite109†mask-image: url(icon.svg#foo) might be pointing to a `<mask id="foo">` element in the SVG document, or be pointing to a `<g id="foo">` element and depending on the cite113†:target pseudo-class to change how it renders as an image.
L140: When this occurs, the "icon.svg" file is loaded up and examined; if the #foo element is indeed a `cite112†mask `, the cite107†url() is treated as a reference to that element; otherwise, it’s interpreted as an image.
